name: German Empire

areaKm2.note: world_1914 German Empire polygon = ~520,000 km2 computed on the sphere (low); published area of the Reich 540,858 km2 (B&H Table 2: 0.5M km2).

population.note: Broadberry and Harrison 2005 Table 2: Germany 1913 = 67.0M (League of Nations 1927). COW NMC v7 tpop 1914 = 67,790k (high). Low = OWID/HYDE Germany 1914 within present-day borders 64.0M, which leaves out Alsace-Lorraine, Posen, West Prussia and Silesia.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share Germany 1910 = 27%, 1920 = 34% (present-day borders). The 1910 census counted 60% in communes of 2,000+ (high) and ~40% in towns of 5,000+ (mid). Low = COW upop/tpop 1914 = 14,279/67,790 = 0.21 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Herwig 1997 ch. 2: after mobilisation (2-18 Aug 1914) the army stood at ~3.82M (peace strength ~761,000 plus reservists), the Feldheer in 7 western and 1 eastern army; plus the navy (~80,000 peace, mobilised higher). The British Army page cites 1.85M and 87 infantry divisions for the field armies alone (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army_during_World_War_I), the low bound of the deployable force. Snapshot month: August 1914. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1914 = 862k, 1915 = 3,823k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Trained men not called up in August: older Landwehr II and Landsturm I classes and partly trained Ersatz reservists. Prewar Germany trained only ~half of each class (Strachan, To Arms ch. 3), so the residual trained pool was smaller than the 5M+ of France proportionally.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Everything outside the P roles: field and foot artillery (~100 artillery regiments), pioneers, signals, trains, staffs, the Ersatz (replacement) units in Germany and the navy (~80,000 peace, ~120,000 mobilised).

mobilizationRatio.note: Total mobilised over the war: 13,250,000 (German government reply to the ILO, 1924) or 11,000,000 (US War Dept) on the cited page; divided by ~67M gives 0.16-0.20.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Infantry of 87 first-line infantry divisions (50 active, 32 reserve, plus Ersatz and Landwehr formations) at ~12,000 rifles each, plus Landwehr brigades and fortress infantry. Reconstruction from the division count (Herwig ch. 2; Strachan ch. 3).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era's best). Evidence: Gewehr 98, ~4,500 MG 08 (Strachan); field-grey uniform; reserve divisions short of artillery

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75 (professional standing army). Evidence: two-year conscripts with a strong NCO corps; reserve divisions used in the front line from day one

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. 18 active Jaeger battalions plus reserve Jaeger battalions (~1,000-1,100 each), attached to cavalry divisions.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: same rifles and MGs, cyclist companies

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: elite rifle battalions recruited from foresters and hunters

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. 11 cavalry divisions in 4 Hoeherer Kavallerie-Kommandos (~5,200 sabres each) plus divisional cavalry squadrons. All German cavalry carried lances and carbines; screening and reconnaissance role, so cavalry_light.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: lance and carbine; obsolescent against MGs and QF artillery

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service regular cavalry

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Herwig, The First World War: Germany and Austria-Hungary (isbn:0-340-57348-1), not read from a fetched source. Field army ~5,000 77 mm FK 96 n.A., ~1,250 10.5 cm leFH 98/09 and ~1,400 heavy pieces of the Fussartillerie (15 cm sFH 02, 21 cm Moerser, a few 42 cm). Fortress guns excluded. Reconstruction from Herwig ch. 2 and Strachan ch. 3.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: the only army with mobile heavy howitzers at corps level; 77 mm inferior to the French 75

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: indirect fire practised, but poor infantry-artillery liaison in 1914

count.note: Cited page: army paper strength ~230 aircraft in August 1914, ~180 usable; plus 12 seaplanes and 1 landplane of the navy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_German_Navy). Unarmed observation two-seaters: no fighters existed in 1914, so all are counted here. Army and navy Zeppelins (~10) not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Taube and Albatros B-types, unarmed

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: Feldflieger-Abteilungen, one per corps, little doctrine for co-operation

count.note: Educated guess. Dreadnought, battlecruiser and pre-dreadnought counts read from the cited Imperial German Navy page; cruiser and destroyer counts recalled from Conway's, not read from a fetched source. Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Cited page: 14 dreadnoughts, 4 battlecruisers and 22 pre-dreadnoughts at the outbreak; plus ~9 armoured and ~40 protected/light cruisers (Conway's 1906-1921, isbn 0-85177-245-5) = 75/85/90, low drops old cruisers and pre-dreadnoughts in reserve; plus high-seas torpedo boats (destroyer equivalents) in service in August 1914, ~90 modern plus ~50 older boats (Conway's 1906-1921; Halpern ch. 1) = 110/140/155. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: the high-seas torpedo boats are torpedo-boat destroyers, moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted (coastal torpedo boats and minesweepers stay excluded).

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.75/0.8/0.85 (85) and high-seas torpedo boats 0.6/0.65/0.7 (140), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.75-1.0 and 0.5-0.75. Evidence: excellent armour subdivision and shells; 28-30.5 cm guns smaller than British 34.3 cm; torpedo boats small and torpedo-heavy, weaker gun armament than British destroyers

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers (85) and high-seas torpedo boats (140), both 0.7/0.75/0.8, role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service petty officers, good gunnery and night-fighting training; intensive night torpedo training

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. U-1 to U-28 commissioned by August 1914, ~24 operational (Conway's 1906-1921; Halpern ch. 1).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era's best). Evidence: diesel U-19 class onwards, early boats paraffin-engined

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: U-9 sank three British cruisers on 22 Sep 1914

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders). Evidence: Great General Staff, mission-type orders; Tannenberg a model encirclement, but Moltke's loss of control at the Marne

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: corps recruited by district, strong NCO corps; reserve divisions held together under heavy losses

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (motivated). Evidence: August 1914 'spirit of 1914' and Burgfrieden; belief in a short defensive war against Russia

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905: magazine rifle, MG, QF artillery). Evidence: Gew 98, MG 08, 21 cm and 42 cm siege mortars; heavy field howitzers ahead of every rival

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars, steel helmet 1915). Evidence: no steel helmet until 1916, no armoured vehicles in service in 1914

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnoughts, steam). Evidence: dreadnoughts with turbines (from Kaiser class), diesel U-boats

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (concrete forts, trenches). Evidence: Feste-group forts at Metz, Strasbourg, Thorn and Koenigsberg

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: mobilisation timetable moved 3.8M men by rail in 17 days; horse-drawn beyond railheads

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (electric telegraph, telephone). Evidence: telephone and telegraph to corps; wireless at army level only; OHL lost touch with the right wing at the Marne

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial reconnaissance (1914). Evidence: Feldflieger-Abteilungen and Zeppelins; aerial reports decisive at Tannenberg

air.note: Anchor: air 7 = 1914 aircraft. Evidence: Taube, Albatros B.I, Aviatik; ~230 aircraft

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): Germany 1913 = 5,815, 1914 = 4,876 (2011 int$). The August snapshot sits between the prewar level and the wartime 1914 average; mid 5,600. B&H Table 2 gives 3,648 in 1990 int$ for the 1913 Reich.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Mid read from Broadberry and Harrison Table 5; low recalled from Ferguson, not read from a fetched source. Low: peacetime defence spending ~3.5% of NNP in 1913 (Ferguson, Pity of War table 6, isbn 0-7139-9246-8). Mid: B&H Table 5 government spending 23.9% of GDP in 1914 (9.8% in 1913) less civil spending, so ~20% military. High: 43.8% government share in 1915.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Strachan, The First World War vol. 1 (isbn:0-19-820877-4), not read from a fetched source. Industry, mining and crafts ~40-45% of NNP in 1913 (Hoffmann series as summarised by Ritschl in Broadberry and Harrison 2005, ch. 2).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Agricultural share of employment c. 1913 assumed ~0.35 (0.32-0.40). Fetched brackets only: agriculture was 32% of net domestic product already in 1895 (Deutsches Kaiserreich, https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsches_Kaiserreich) and 29% of employment in 1937 (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agrarwirtschaft_und_Agrarpolitik_im_Deutschen_Reich_(1933%E2%80%931945)). Germany imported ~1/5 of its food before 1914 (B&H overview, qualitative).

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Strachan, The First World War vol. 1 (isbn:0-19-820877-4), not read from a fetched source. Men reaching 20 per year: ~1.9M births per year in the 1890s, half male, ~65% survival to 20 gives ~0.6M; only ~half were trained before 1913 (Strachan ch. 3).

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Single-seat fighters per year 1915-1917, a share of total German aircraft output recalled as ~4,500 (1915), ~8,200 (1916), ~19,700 (1917) from Morrow, The Great War in the Air (not fetched); fighter share is a split by judgement.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Two-seat reconnaissance, ground-attack and bomber aircraft per year 1915-1917, the remainder of the totals recalled from Morrow (see fighters).

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns per year 1915-1918; the 1916 Hindenburg Programme aimed at ~3,000 guns per month.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Capital ships, cruisers and destroyers completed per year. Capital ships and cruisers 1914-1916 = 3/5/8: 3 Koenig class and Derfflinger in late 1914, 2 Bayern and Luetzow 1916, ~6 light cruisers per year; torpedo boats (destroyers) 1915-1918 = 30/45/60 (Conway's 1906-1921). Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

submarines.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. U-boats commissioned per year: ~52 (1915), 108 (1916), ~87 (1917) (Conway's 1906-1921; Halpern).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Chausseen (metalled highways) and lesser engineered roads of the Reich.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Hamburg, Bremen/Bremerhaven, Wilhelmshaven, Kiel, Danzig, Stettin, Koenigsberg, Luebeck, Emden.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register returns 1914 (steam and sail vessels of 100 tons gross and over owned, Register Book 1913-14): Germany 5,082,061 GRT, of which steam 4,743,046. High = published 1914 total of ~5.46M GRT. Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Recalled from van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-21730-X), not read from a fetched source. van Creveld, Supplying War ch. 4: the right wing outran its railheads by ~150-300 km by the Marne; horse transport sustained ~25 km/day for a few weeks.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Strachan, The First World War vol. 1 (isbn:0-19-820877-4), not read from a fetched source. Reich horse census ~4.5M in 1913; ~715,000 horses requisitioned on mobilisation (Strachan ch. 3).

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified cities (Metz, Strasbourg, Koenigsberg), population support; no climate depth.

notes: Snapshot date August 1914 after mobilisation (order of 1 Aug; Feldheer concentrated by 17-18 Aug). Territory and population = the German Empire in Europe incl. Alsace-Lorraine; colonies (10.7M people, B&H Table 2) excluded and not listed in includes. Forces are the whole army; the western deployment was ~1.6M men in 7 armies and the eastern 8th Army ~150,000-200,000. Aircraft are all counted as aircraft_strike because no fighters existed in 1914. Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, cruisers and destroyers (incl. high-seas torpedo boats) = ships_major, coastal torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Book figures (Herwig, Strachan, Conway's) are from standard works not fetched online, graded at most B.
